topic: Nanami's one proven edge over Mahito, surviving a direct hit in chapter 23, is exactly what Shibuya spends chapters stripping away before the rematch
title: Nanami's One Edge On Mahito Was Gone By Shibuya
description: Nanami Kento only ever beat Mahito once, back in chapter 23, and that one detail explains everything that happens later. Shibuya spends chapters 92 through 120 stripping away the exact advantage that saved him then, before Mahito ever gets a second shot at him. From the full story: Nanami Was Never Supposed To Survive Shibuya.
comment: Was Nanami's fate sealed the moment Gojo got sealed away, or did his own choices put him there? Pick one.

lines.text: Nanami beat Mahito exactly once. Shibuya made sure it never happened again.

shot.fallback: weary swordsman facing a smiling curse spirit in a wrecked station

lines.text: In chapter 23, Mahito landed a direct hit on Nanami's soul, and nobody who'd taken that hit before ever walked away.

shot.fallback: clawed curse hand reaching toward a swordsman

lines.text: Nanami did. That one detail is the whole reason Mahito called him exceptionally strong.

shot.fallback: weary swordsman still standing after a brutal hit

lines.text: Carry that fact into Shibuya, because the story spends eight chapters erasing it...

shot.fallback: swordsman walking toward a chaotic city street

lines.text: Dagon takes his eye in chapter 106. Jogo burns half his body in chapter 120.

shot.fallback: swordsman scorched and battered mid battle

lines.text: His whole team ends up too hurt to stand beside him.

shot.fallback: two fallen fighters lying in a dark hallway

lines.text: By the time Mahito finds him again, the body that survived him once has nothing left to survive with.

shot.fallback: exhausted swordsman facing a calm curse spirit

lines.text: No eye. No team. Half his skin already gone.
This isn't bad luck. It's the manga spending chapters removing the one reason Nanami ever survived Mahito before.
Because Nanami beat Mahito exactly once...

shot.fallback: swordsman confronting a stitched curse in an alley
